controlling_finding.title: The loss class is embodiment-authored and uncalibrated; Cold Review 003 §3.5 reconstructs
controlling_finding.mechanism: SP-151 draws the loss class from THE EMBODIMENT'S OWN published capability declaration. No clause closes that vocabulary and no clause individuates 'capability'. SP-151's sentence 'Two embodiments lacking different capabilities therefore carry different loss classes' is an assertion about the world, not a constraint the program enforces.
controlling_finding.reconstruction: CR-003 §3.5's pair G′ (cannot hold a second pending contribution) and H′ (can hold two but cannot preserve canonical order) may each TRUTHFULLY publish the same coarse loss class — e.g. SECOND_RECORD_UNSUPPORTED. SP-155 veridicality is satisfied by both, because the declaration is true of both. SP-152 therefore compares them EQUAL, and the loss of canonical ordering — a member of P-L1-A's sealed scope list — is again invisible.
controlling_finding.why_it_is_blocking: v0.4 §16.2 rates the CR3-04 repair IMPOSSIBLE. It is not impossible; it is unenforced. This is the founder's own standard failing: 'A repair counts only if the normative representation either makes the defect impossible or makes it explicitly detectable.' The hole was moved from an undefined token to an uncalibrated vocabulary.
controlling_finding.author_verification: CONFIRMED INDEPENDENTLY BY THE AUTHOR-SIDE SELFSYSTEM. Searched v0.4 for individuat / granularity / which-capability — zero occurrences. Of 19 'loss class' lines, none enumerates or bounds the vocabulary.

author_side_verification_of_the_review.principle: The reviewer's load-bearing claims were re-derived against machine state before relay. A review is not evidence merely because it is independent.

cr4_03_confirmed_and_owned.claim: The auditor published in v0.4 §16.4 does not execute, and its body is duplicated with a divergent copy.
cr4_03_confirmed_and_owned.verification: Extracted the fenced block verbatim and ran it. `SyntaxError: unterminated string literal` at document line 781. The block contains the script TWICE: a complete correct copy at document lines 666–780, then a truncated second copy at 781–869 whose first line lost the prefix `norm_nofence = re.sub(r'^` at the splice seam. The two copies differ at exactly one point — the FT row regex, head `^\| FT-\d{2} · ` versus tail `^\| FT-\d{2} ` — which is the very defect the author had corrected, reintroduced by the duplicate.
cr4_03_confirmed_and_owned.ownership: This defect is the author's, introduced during SP-R04, and is the SAME splice-boundary error class as the earlier §17 mis-cut in that movement. It recurred undetected because the author verified the auditor's OUTPUT and never verified that the PUBLISHED BYTES execute.
cr4_03_confirmed_and_owned.aggravating: §16.5 states the block was 'Produced by running the §16.4 script against this file.' As published, that is false — no such run is possible. §16.5 exists because CR3-17 caught v0.3 mis-transcribing generated evidence; the successor defect is worse in kind, being a provenance claim rather than a formatting one.

cr4_03_countervailing_fact.verification: Ran the head copy against v0.4 and byte-compared its stdout to the published block. BYTE-IDENTICAL: True. The diff-mode block against v0.3 also reproduces (ROWS_ADDED 12 · ROWS_REMOVED 0 · ROWS_CHANGED 21 · UNMARKED_CHANGED_ROWS NONE).
cr4_03_countervailing_fact.consequence: The numbers are true; their stated provenance is not. Cold Review 003's overstatement finding does NOT recur. The repair is transcriptional, not arithmetical.

cr4_02_confirmed.claim: The required vector does not determine its own reference trace on the DaySlot coordinate.
cr4_02_confirmed.verification: SP-094 pins three of SP-019's seven L-facts — state idle, empty durable Entry history, empty pending. Ledger identity, Ritual identity, canonical history order and the CURRENT DAYSLOT ORDINAL are unpinned. SP-023 declares the DaySlot ordinal SEMANTIC. Two conforming runs of the sole required vector at different DaySlot ordinals therefore fail SP-091 equality with no clause violated, and SP-093 normalization cannot erase a coordinate SP-023 made semantic.

what_v04_got_right: Recorded so the record is not one-sided. The blocker is genuinely closed by mechanism. §16.5's tallies are accurate and byte-reproducible. SP-090 is exact and survived all nine entailment attacks. CR3-09, CR3-13, CR3-16 and CR3-18 are mechanically closed. The EXACT set is fully enumerable and fully audited for the first time. §18.2's declared residuals are honest, and §12.2's refusal to overstate FT-11's closure is the right posture.

reviewer_self_limitation.asymmetry: The reviewer's POSITIVE results — the CR4-01 trace, the CR4-02 construction, the CR4-03 SyntaxError and byte-diff, the CR4-04/05 byte comparisons against extracted L1 — are re-verifiable by anyone in minutes and do not depend on its reasoning being sound. Its NEGATIVE results — six CR3-B01 attacks surviving, silent capability loss remaining impossible, capability ≠ permission preserved, L/T non-interference holding — are WEAK evidence, because it may share the author's blind spots.
reviewer_self_limitation.consequence_for_cr3_b01: CR3-B01 CLOSED is a negative result and therefore carries the weaker evidential weight. It is closed against everything a lineage-independent reviewer could construct. A model-independent or external review could plausibly break what this one could not.
reviewer_self_limitation.not_tested: RealityIR, emitter, oracle and target-layer questions; commission procedural conformance beyond cited clauses; exhaustive auditor mutation search; v0.1 and v0.2 beyond digests. The CR3-07 content-value-domain residual rests on positing a sentinel and was flagged rather than graded.
reviewer_self_limitation.near_false_positive_disclosed: The reviewer nearly recorded §18's HBC line as a defect because it fails against the governance repository. HBC is a separate child repository at projects/hbc-html where the claim verifies exactly — HEAD e350205f, 30 tracked, 0 modified, 0 staged. The finding was killed. RUORA nests many independent repositories; a HEAD from one looks like a nonexistent commit in another.
